analysis.title: CIO View: Emerging market equities
key_insights: UBS CIO moves EM equities to Neutral from Attractive, citing normalizing earnings growth (63% in 2026 to 20% in 2027) and rising risks to US exports.
New MSCI EM index targets: 1700 for June 2027 and 1770 for December 2027. The index stood at 1,560 on 16 Nov 2026.

Global AI capex stays supportive in 2027, with Taiwan and Korea the main beneficiaries of the AI supply chain. The 2028 capex outlook is less certain because of the Fed's rate-hiking cycle, AI financing questions and uncertainty after the US midterm elections.
Taiwan is cut to Neutral and Korea stays Neutral, since the US is a key export market for both.

Asia ex-Japan and EM earnings are expected to grow 72% and 63% in 2026, then 20% each in 2027, the highest rate globally. Both trade at 8.0x 12-month forward P/E after the recent correction, well below historical levels.

Subsiding risk of aggressive Fed hikes and lower oil prices are a positive backdrop, but recent volatility and the risk of slower AI capex make near-term risk-reward more balanced. UBS advises avoiding single-stock concentration and diversifying.

China H-shares remain tied to US equity volatility. Internet platform valuations have already corrected over three months, which cushions the downside. Negative earnings revisions are the main constraint on a rerating over the next 3-6 months.

UBS prefers China A-shares over H-shares. Government-backed capital purchases and stabilization measures since October 2026 have set a floor for valuations, and parts of the semiconductor and AI supply chains have corrected substantially. Health care (earnings growth) and financials (dividend yields) are suggested as additions beyond tech.

Southeast Asia remains constructive for 2027 with more differentiation across markets. Singapore is preferred, Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines are Neutral, and Indonesia is cautious because of policy uncertainty and the risk of an MSCI reclassification, which could cause selling in equities and the currency.

Asian AI supply chain EPS should grow strongly in 2027, but investors will increasingly focus on possible capex cuts in 2028 and beyond. UBS favors Taiwanese foundries, Japan's platform companies and mainland China internet platforms with strong core businesses and accelerating cloud growth.

Latin America offers diversification through commodities, infrastructure and domestic cyclicals. Brazil's domestic market is expected to stay under pressure after the election result, with slowing growth and higher-for-longer local rates. Further repricing could create entry points in commodity exporters, but UBS sees limited near-term catalysts.
Scenario targets for MSCI EM in December 2027 are 2,100 in the upside case and 1,250 in the downside case.

sector_views.rationale: UBS sees an attractive earnings growth profile and suggests selectively adding exposure.
2027 capex supports strong EPS growth, but 2028 capex cuts, monetization and financing are open questions, so UBS asks for selectivity and risk discipline.
Further repricing in Brazil could create entry points in commodity exporters, but there are limited catalysts for a sustained rebound now.

earnings_insights: MSCI EM earnings are expected to grow 63% in 2026 and 20% in 2027 (UBS forecast).
MSCI Asia ex-Japan earnings are expected to grow 72% in 2026 and 20% in 2027 (UBS forecast).
Asia's AI supply chain is expected to post strong EPS growth in 2027 on another year of rising capex (UBS forecast).
Negative earnings revisions in China H-shares are the main factor limiting a sustained rerating over the next 3-6 months.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Earnings growth is expected to normalize sharply in 2027, which is part of the reason for the downgrade to Neutral.
Still the highest rate globally, but well below 2026.
Strong 2026 growth is driven by the AI supply chain.
Valuation is well below historical levels after the correction, which limits downside.
Implies upside from the 1,560 level of 16 Nov 2026.

macro_indicators.indicator: MSCI EM index scenario targets, Dec 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: The scenario range is skewed to the downside relative to the 1,560 level.

risk_factors: A slowdown or cut in AI capex in 2028 and beyond, with open questions on AI monetization and financing.
The Federal Reserve's rate-hiking cycle and tighter financial conditions, including a persistently stronger dollar.
Further tariffs, export controls or policy uncertainty disrupting trade.
Prolonged energy supply shocks keeping inflation high and hurting energy-importing EMs.
Limited or narrowly targeted Chinese fiscal support leading to a derating and outflows.
Negative earnings revisions capping a China H-share rerating.
Brazil's slowing growth and higher-for-longer local rates.
vol_and_positioning: Near-term volatility in US equities is likely to remain a key driver of China H-share sentiment, and market swings could persist over the coming months.
UBS advises avoiding single-stock concentration risk in Asia and EM equities and diversifying across the range of opportunities.
MSCI's potential reclassification of Indonesia could put selling pressure on its equity market and currency.
geopolitical: Risks to US exports from tariffs, export controls and policy uncertainty.
US midterm elections create uncertainty for the 2028 AI capex outlook.
Energy supply disruptions and geopolitical trade tensions are named as downside risks, with their resolution as an upside scenario.
Brazil's election result is weighing on its domestic market.
MSCI's potential reclassification of the MSCI Indonesia Index.
Central-government-backed capital purchases and stabilization measures in China since October 2026.

tension_points.bull_case: Global AI capex stays supportive in 2027, and another year of rising capex should drive strong EPS growth in Asia's AI supply chain, with Taiwan and Korea key beneficiaries.
tension_points.bear_case: The 2028 capex outlook is less certain because of the Fed's rate-hiking cycle, AI financing questions and uncertainty after the US midterm elections, and investors are likely to focus on capex cuts in 2028 and beyond.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings growth normalizes and AI capex risk makes near-term risk-reward more balanced.
theme_stances.evidence: the near-term risk-reward appears more balanced

theme_stances.key_argument: Domestic market support since October 2026 has helped establish a floor for A-share valuations.
theme_stances.evidence: We continue to prefer China A-shares over H-shares.
